findings.claim: Passing `input: arg1` directly forwards a `skipToken` sentinel into `trpcSubscriptionOptions` as the subscription input, which the previous queryKey-derived path filtered out
findings.rationale: `getQueryKeyInternal` deliberately excludes `skipToken` (and `undefined`) from the serialized key, so before this change the subscription helper could never observe a raw `skipToken` as input. Now the raw first argument is handed through unchanged. If `trpcSubscriptionOptions` does not explicitly special-case `skipToken` (e.g. to disable the subscription rather than send it over the wire), a `skipToken` value would be serialized and sent to the server. Worth verifying the downstream handler branches on `input === skipToken`. Medium confidence — this may well be exactly the bug the change intends to fix, but it is the main behavioral risk introduced.

findings.claim: The input is now supplied twice (as `input` and inside `queryKey`), creating two sources of truth that can silently diverge
findings.rationale: `input: arg1` and `getQueryKeyInternal({ input: arg1 })` both encode the same value, but the key path normalizes/strips values (undefined, skipToken) while the direct field does not. If `trpcSubscriptionOptions` internally still reads the input off `queryKey[1]?.input` in some code paths, the two can disagree and produce a subscription whose cache key does not match the data actually requested. Low-to-medium confidence without seeing `trpcSubscriptionOptions`; suggest deriving one from the other.
